```python
# Test basic wrapping
assert wrap_("hello world", 10) == ["hello", "world"], (wrap_("hello world", 10), ["hello", "world"])

# Test when text fits in one line
assert wrap_("hello", 10) == ["hello"], (wrap_("hello", 10), ["hello"])

# Test exact fit
assert wrap_("hello world", 11) == ["hello world"], (wrap_("hello world", 11), ["hello world"])

# Test multiple words wrapping
assert wrap_("one two three four", 10) == ["one two", "three four"], (wrap_("one two three four", 10), ["one two", "three four"])

# Test empty string
assert wrap_("", 10) == [], (wrap_("", 10), [])

# Test whitespace only
assert wrap_("   ", 10) == [], (wrap_("   ", 10), [])

# Test tabs expansion (tab = 8 spaces)
# "a\tb" becomes "a       b" (a + 8 spaces + b = 10 chars)
assert wrap_("a\tb", 10) == ["a       b"], (wrap_("a\tb", 10), ["a       b"])

# Test tabs with wrapping
# "a\tb c" becomes "a       b c" (11 chars), width 10
# "a       b" is 9 chars, "c" is 1 char
assert wrap_("a\tb c", 10) == ["a       b", "c"], (wrap_("a\tb c", 10), ["a       b", "c"])

# Test whitespace collapsing
# "hello   world" becomes "hello world"
assert wrap_("hello   world", 10) == ["hello", "world"], (wrap_("hello   world", 10), ["hello", "world"])

# Test multiple whitespace types
# "hello\nworld\tfoo" becomes "hello world foo"
assert wrap_("hello\nworld\tfoo", 10) == ["hello", "world foo"], (wrap_("hello\nworld\tfoo", 10), ["hello", "world foo"])

# Test word longer than width is broken
# "abcdefghij" is 10 chars, width 5
assert wrap_("abcdefghij", 5) == ["abcde", "fghij"], (wrap_("abcdefghij", 5), ["abcde", "fghij"])

# Test word longer than width with other words
# "hi abcdefghij" with width 5
# "hi" fits, then "abcdefghij" is broken into "abcde", "fghij"
assert wrap_("hi abcdefghij", 5) == ["hi", "abcde", "fghij"], (wrap_("hi abcdefghij", 5), ["hi", "abcde", "fghij"])

# Test word exactly width
assert wrap_("abcde", 5) == ["abcde"], (wrap_("abcde", 5), ["abcde"])

# Test word width+1
assert wrap_("abcdef", 5) == ["abcde", "f"], (wrap_("abcdef", 5), ["abcde", "f"])

# Test multiple long words
# "abcdefg hijk" with width 4
# "abcdefg" broken into "abcd", "efg"
# "hijk" fits in 4
assert wrap_("abcdefg hijk", 4) == ["abcd", "efg", "hijk"], (wrap_("abcdefg hijk", 4), ["abcd", "efg", "hijk"])

# Test width 1
assert wrap_("ab cd", 1) == ["a", "b", "c", "d"], (wrap_("ab cd", 1), ["a", "b", "c", "d"])

# Test leading/trailing whitespace stripped
assert wrap_("  hello world  ", 10) == ["hello", "world"], (wrap_("  hello world  ", 10), ["hello", "world"])

# Test newlines in input are treated as whitespace
assert wrap_("hello\nworld", 10) == ["hello", "world"], (wrap_("hello\nworld", 10), ["hello", "world"])

# Test mixed tabs and spaces
# "a \t b" -> expand tab: "a        b" (a + space + 8 spaces + space + b = 12 chars)
# Wait: "a \t b" = 'a', ' ', '\t', ' ', 'b'
# After tab expansion: 'a', ' ', '        ', ' ', 'b' = "a         b" (11 chars)
# After collapse: "a b" (3 chars)
assert wrap_("a \t b", 10) == ["a b"], (wrap_("a \t b", 10), ["a b"])

# Test that lines are never longer than width (except unbreakable chunks)
# "aaaaa bbbbb" with width 5
assert wrap_("aaaaa bbbbb", 5) == ["aaaaa", "bbbbb"], (wrap_("aaaaa bbbbb", 5), ["aaaaa", "bbbbb"])

# Test complex case
# "The quick brown fox" with width 10
# "The quick" = 9, "brown fox" = 9
assert wrap_("The quick brown fox", 10) == ["The quick", "brown fox"], (wrap_("The quick brown fox", 10), ["The quick", "brown fox"])

# Test with width 0 - this is an edge case, but let's see
# Actually width 0 would mean every char is its own line for long words
# But for normal words, they can't fit. Let's test with a single char
assert wrap_("a", 0) == ["a"], (wrap_("a", 0), ["a"])
```

```python
def wrap_(text, width):

    expanded = text.replace('\t', ' ' * 8)
    
    # Collapse whitespace: replace any sequence of whitespace with a single space
    # Then strip leading/trailing whitespace
    import re
    collapsed = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', expanded).strip()

        return []

    words = collapsed.split(' ')

    current_length = 0

                current_line = []
                current_length = 0

            i = 0

                chunk = word[i:i + width]
                lines.append(chunk)
                i += width

                current_line = [word]
                current_length = len(word)
    
    # Flush the last line
    if current_line:
        lines.append(' '.join(current_line))
    
    return lines
```
